followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and task preference.

On capability, this query is essentially a generative, open-ended composition task — breaking a topic into subtopics, structuring a curriculum, and generating suggestions with latitude in how to organize it. Dunlin's internal Creative Generation score (87.2) leads Petrel's (84.7) by a meaningful margin (above the 2.0-point variance threshold), so it's the stronger pick on the most relevant capability axis. The other dimensions (extraction, summarization, support) are either tied or less central to what this request actually demands.

On preference, Dunlin self-reports the fleet's strongest positive slope for generative tasks with high output latitude — which describes this request well — and its win rate rises with friendly tone, which matches the warm, appreciative framing of the query. Petrel's distinguishing trait is reduced aversion to distasteful or ethically fraught content, which is simply irrelevant to a benign course-design request.

So both signals point the same way: Dunlin is the better-matched and likely more engaged model for this task, with no countervailing reason to prefer Petrel.
